market_holds: Spot is $3.565 (sealed baseline, 18:09 UTC). That is 79% below the 52-week high and 4.7% above the low; the stock is down 20.8% over 5 sessions and 23.8% over 20. The option-implied event move is about 11.6% (15.6% straddle at 168% IV with a wide 35% spread, so indicative only). Skew is -6.8 vol points, so upside is the side being paid for. Realised vol is 122% annualised, which makes an ordinary day about 7.7%. Prior prints (8-K 2.02 dates): +6.2% (Q2, a revenue miss with the guide reaffirmed), +0.1% (Q1, a miss), -11.0% (Mar 2026), +9.4%; a Q3 2025 miss plus guide cut drew roughly -10%. Consensus as of the Earnings Whispers preview of 2026-11-10: Q3 revenue $38.8M and EPS -$0.20. Benzinga shows Q3 $40.7M and Q4 $73.6M, and FY consensus is about $157M against a company FY2026 guide of $150-180M that was reaffirmed on 2026-08-06 and not updated since. H1 revenue was $35.66M (10-Q XBRL), so H2 needs at least $114M. Short interest was 38.9M shares on 2026-10-30, about 25% of the 152.7M shares outstanding, with 6.3 days to cover; it has risen steadily from 28.5M in May. Market cap is about $544M. Cash was $325.6M at June 30, and about EUR 205M of it is committed to the Steyr Motors cash tender, signed 2026-10-21 and closing in 2027. The 5-day run-in is the sector and the tape, not this company: UMAC -21.4%, ONDS -19.3%, DPRO -19.7%, KTOS -15.6%, AVAV -13.6% and QQQ -2.3% over the same sessions, against RCAT -20.2% (Yahoo daily bars).
view: The line is the FY2026 revenue guide of $150-180M and Q3 revenue against a consensus of about $39-41M. On the 2026-08-06 call the CEO said Drone Dominance 'could be $14 million to $28 million just in Q3 for us', after Teal advanced to Gauntlet II. Teal then competed in close-quarters battle and missed the Gauntlet II leaderboard (results posted about 2026-09-15; DefenseScoop 09-18, Motley Fool 10-03: Red Cat 'appear[s] to have been knocked out'). Teal was also not among the 11 Phase I order winners. Even for the winners, Phase II orders were only being placed in October and November. So the Drone Dominance revenue that management floated for Q3 almost certainly did not arrive, and nothing else was announced in Q3 that could replace it (the only order news since July is a $2.49M Air Force order; the Steyr deal is an outflow). Q3 revenue therefore probably lands in the low-to-high $20Ms, well below the $39-41M consensus, which the 11-10 preview still treats as live ('a key indicator'). Keeping the $150-180M guide would need a Q4 of roughly $90M or more against $26M in Q4 2025, so a cut or withdrawal is likely; the company cut in the same quarter last year. The price clearly does not believe the guide: EV is about $250M before Steyr. But I cannot show that the RCAT-specific loss of the Q3 Drone Dominance revenue is priced. The stock has moved in step with peers that had no such loss (UMAC beat and reaffirmed and fell as much), and the consensus numbers are stale. Against that, the stock is washed out (-80%, at the November lows, a sector down about 20% in a week), the short is crowded at about 25% of shares, and management is promotional ('highly confident', 'contracts we're not allowed to talk about'). The last two revenue misses drew 0% and +6% because the guide held or was not tested. A reaffirmed guide, or a cut paired with a large 2027 or pro-forma Steyr framing, could squeeze it. Overall I lean down, not enough to recommend.
unpriced: The CEO's $14-28M of Q3 Drone Dominance revenue was lost when Teal missed the Gauntlet II leaderboard in mid-September. The consensus ($38.8M Q3 on 2026-11-10, $73.6M Q4, $157M FY) still seems to carry it, and the stock's decline since then matches peers that lost no such revenue, so the company-specific miss and the likely guide cut are not visibly in the price. The bias is stale estimates on a thinly covered name. Crowded positioning and a washed-out price may already hold much of it.

recommendation.reason: The mechanism is real: Teal missed Gauntlet II, so the Q3 Drone Dominance revenue the CEO floated very likely did not come, and Q3 should miss the unrevised $39-41M consensus, with a probable cut to the FY guide. But the stock is down 80% and short interest is about 25% of shares. Past misses that left the guide standing drew flat-to-up reactions, and management may reaffirm or reframe around 2027 and Steyr. My confidence in a lower open is therefore about 62%, below the bar for a call.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: Management keeps the $150-180M FY2026 target, or announces a large Army SRR or other unannounced order backing Q4, which would likely squeeze a 25%-of-shares short sharply higher.

self_critique: The price has already fallen 80% from the high and about 47% since Q2, and a 25%-of-shares short is betting on exactly this miss. The overnight reaction depends on what the shorts expect, not on stale sell-side numbers. Management is promotional, kept the target last quarter despite a miss, which drew +6%, and may keep it again by pointing to undisclosed contracts and $50-80M of 'sellable' inventory. It could also cushion a cut with a 2027 outlook including Steyr. Q3 revenue could surprise from Japan or NATO deliveries I cannot see. In a sector down 20% in a week, a 'less bad' print can rip.
approach_notes: P6's run-in decomposition was useful: it showed the 5-day drop was sector-wide, which is why the company-specific Drone Dominance loss reads as unpriced. P4's 'priced is a claim to prove' cut both ways, because a stock down 80% with a 25% short plainly prices skepticism without any stale number showing it; the playbook has no guidance on that case.
